question: Which event has the lowest cost?
evidence: event refers to event_name; lowest cost means MIN(cost)
clarification: If several rows tie at the cut-off, return all of them.
gold: SELECT c0 FROM (SELECT T1.event_name AS c0, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY T3.cost) AS __r FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event INNER JOIN expense AS T3 ON T2.budget_id = T3.link_to_budget) AS __t WHERE __r <= 1
gold0: SELECT T1.event_name FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event INNER JOIN expense AS T3 ON T2.budget_id = T3.link_to_budget ORDER BY T3.cost LIMIT 1

b.request: Return the event name of every event whose associated expense has the minimum cost across all expenses, including all events tied at that cost
b.sql: SELECT e.event_name FROM event AS e WHERE e.event_id IN (SELECT b.link_to_event FROM budget AS b JOIN expense AS x ON x.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE x.cost = (SELECT MIN(cost) FROM expense))

c.request:
Which event has the lowest cost?
Evidence: event refers to event_name; lowest cost means MIN(cost)
If several rows tie at the cut-off, return all of them.
c.sql: SELECT DISTINCT e.event_name FROM event AS e JOIN budget AS b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id JOIN expense AS x ON x.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE x.cost = (SELECT MIN(cost) FROM expense)

d.request: Which event names have the minimum cost? Return all rows tied at that cost.
d.sql: SELECT e.event_name FROM event AS e JOIN budget AS b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id JOIN expense AS x ON x.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE x.cost = (SELECT MIN(cost) FROM expense)
